audit_note: CRB gives water and unchanged sulfuric acid; SynRXN represents the same overall composition as sulfate, protons, and hydroxide. The distinction is mainly acid-base bookkeeping.
CRB represents DIPEA and fluoride as an ammonium-fluoride salt; SynRXN leaves neutral DIPEA and HF.
The POCl3-mediated chlorination admits different formal phosphorus-containing coproducts; the specific hydrolysis state is not established by this record.
CRB accounts for stoichiometric SOCl2 consumption as SO2 and two HCl; SynRXN gives water and carries SOCl2 through unchanged.
CRB accounts for HATU consumption with tetramethylurea and an HOAt-derived species; SynRXN gives water and carries HATU through unchanged.

CRB gives water and neutral sodium; SynRXN gives an explicit hydrogen species, hydroxide, and sodium ion. These are alternative formal balance representations; neither establishes isolated coproducts.
The completions use different carbonate, bicarbonate, hydroxide, and water bookkeeping; duplicated spectator carbonate in CRB makes the detailed coproduct assignment uncertain.
CRB gives sulfonate plus bicarbonate; SynRXN gives sulfonic acid plus carbonate, differing by proton transfer.
CRB gives mesylate plus bicarbonate; SynRXN gives methanesulfonic acid plus carbonate, differing by proton transfer.
CRB gives silyl mesylate; SynRXN gives hydrolysed silanol and methanesulfonic acid after adding water.
CRB predicts methane, whereas SynRXN adds an oxygen species and gives methanol; methanol is the more plausible methoxy-derived coproduct, although the oxygen source is unspecified.
